raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

DeepSeek-V4 fails at engine init with `--linear-backend marlin` (#60587) or `triton`. `deep_gemm_fp8_o_proj` reads `wo_a.weight` directly and only understands the grouped `[g, r, d]` FP8 layout that the DeepGEMM linear kernels leave behind. Other backends lay the weight out for their own GEMM. This PR dequantizes such a `wo_a` to BF16 after loading so the existing BF16 bmm branch handles it.

Fixes #60587.

## Claims

- DeepSeek-V4-Flash starts and generates with `--linear-backend marlin` and `--linear-backend triton` (both crashed in `_o_proj` during profiling before).
- With real weights, GSM8K under `--linear-backend marlin` matches the default backend (table below).
- Default path (DeepGEMM / FlashInfer-DeepGEMM kernels) is unchanged: `wo_a` is already the 3D FP8 tensor, so the new hook returns early.

## Validation

New test in `tests/quantization/test_fp8.py`: builds a block-FP8 `wo_a` under `linear_backend` in {marlin, triton}, runs the kernel's `process_weights_after_loading`, then `deep_gemm_fp8_o_proj`, and compares with an FP32 reference.

```bash
pytest tests/quantization/test_fp8.py -k test_deepseek_v4_o_proj_with_non_deep_gemm_wo_a
```

1xH100: 2 passed. With the `maybe_dequant_wo_a` call removed from the test, both fail: marlin with `Expected size for first two dimensions of batch2 tensor to be: [2, 512] but got: [2, 128]` (same error as #60587), triton with DeepGEMM's `layout.hpp:46: t.dim() == N`.

E2E on 1xH100, `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash` with dummy weights, `hf_overrides={"n_routed_experts": 8}`, `enforce_eager=True`, 2 prompts x 16 tokens:

| `linear_backend` | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| auto (FlashInfer-DeepGEMM) | ok | ok |
| deep_gemm | ok | ok |
| marlin | `RuntimeError: Expected size for first two dimensions of batch2 tensor to be: [8, 4096] but got: [8, 1024].` | ok |
| triton | DeepGEMM `layout.hpp:46: t.dim() == N` in `fp8_einsum` | ok |
| cutlass | `dispatch_scaled_mm ... scaled_mm_helper.hpp:17` | same, see below |
| torch | `Invalid scaling configuration.` | same, see below |

SM100 FlashInfer layer (RopeQuant recheck), 1xB200, same dummy setup reshaped to 128 local heads / 16 `wo_a` groups so RopeQuant applies, `kv_cache_dtype="fp8"`, `attention_backend="FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV4"`:

| run | result |
|---|---|
| auto | RopeQuant on, ok |
| marlin, this PR | RopeQuant chosen in `__init__`, turned off after `wo_a` becomes BF16, ok |
| marlin, this PR minus the `_fuse_rope_quant` recheck line | `assert use_fp8` in `deep_gemm_fp8_o_proj` |

GSM8K, real weights, 2xH200, TP=2, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8 --block-size 256 --max-model-len 8192`, `tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --num-questions 1319 --num-shots 5`:

| `linear_backend` | code | GSM8K | invalid |
|---|---|---|---|
| auto (FlashInfer-DeepGEMM, FP8 `wo_a`) | this PR (path unchanged) | 0.9492 | 0.0 |
| marlin | this PR (BF16 `wo_a`) | 0.9484 | 0.0 |

One run each, greedy; the gap is 1 question out of 1319. I did not rerun main with real weights; the main failure is the dummy-weight row above. Per-GPU model memory goes from 73.8 GiB to 74.52 GiB with the BF16 `wo_a`.

## Details

Root cause: `wo_a` is a `ColumnParallelLinear` marked `is_bmm`, but it is never called. `deep_gemm_fp8_o_proj` takes `wo_a.weight` (and its scale) and feeds them to `fp8_einsum`, or to a BF16 `bmm` when the weight is not FP8. Only `DeepGemmFp8BlockScaledMMKernel.process_weights_after_loading` (also used by the FlashInfer-DeepGEMM kernel) reshapes the weight to `[g, r, d]` with DeepGEMM scales. The kernel is picked in `create_weights`, before `is_bmm` is set, and `--linear-backend` applies to every FP8 linear, so `wo_a` can end up in Marlin's packed int32 layout or a plain 2D FP8 tensor.

The fix is local to the three CUDA attention layers that call `deep_gemm_fp8_o_proj` (FlashMLA, FlashInfer SM100, FlashInfer SM120). Their new `process_weights_after_loading` runs after every quant method's own processing (deferred attention layers), and calls `maybe_dequant_wo_a`, which uses `get_and_maybe_dequant_weights` (same helper MLA uses for `kv_b_proj`). For Marlin and the DeepGEMM-capable platforms it dequantizes through the kernel's own `apply`, so it does not depend on each backend's layout. ROCm/XPU/CPU subclasses are untouched since their `wo_a` paths differ. On the SM100 FlashInfer layer, RopeQuant was decided in `__init__` against the not-yet-loaded FP8 weight, so it is rechecked after the swap.

Tradeoffs: on non-DeepGEMM backends `wo_a` is held in BF16 (4096x8192 per layer, about 1.5 GB more for DeepSeek-V4-Flash at TP=1, split across TP ranks) and that projection runs as a BF16 bmm. The default backend keeps the FP8 path.

Limitations:
- `cutlass` and `torch` still fail before reaching `_o_proj`: their block-FP8 GEMMs reject the checkpoint's UE8M0 scales (#47988 covers CUTLASS/Triton E8M0 handling). Out of scope here.
- The reporter is on GB10 (SM121), which I don't have. I validated on H100/H200. The SM120 layer gets the same hook.

Not a duplicate:
- #56119 (open, last updated 09-24, merge conflicts, no review) dequantizes `is_bmm` weights inside `Fp8LinearMethod` only when Marlin is selected. This PR keeps shared FP8 code untouched and covers any backend that leaves `wo_a` outside the DeepGEMM layout: Triton is verified above; B12x (used by the GB10 recipe) also keeps a plain 2D FP8 weight and takes the same path, not run.
- #55172 adds a BF16 helper for SM8x. I applied its `o_proj.py` on H100 with `--linear-backend marlin` and it still fails (`marlin_gemm ... a.size(1) = 32768, size_k = 4096`), because it infers the group width from the packed Marlin weight.
- #41834 (SM12x enablement, open since May) makes Marlin refuse block-FP8 layers instead.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to find the root cause, write the change and run the validation above.

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.
Hi @ischencheng, keeping the fix in the DSv4 code without a DeepGEMM dependency is what GB10 needs. The issue was reported on 2x GB10 with `--linear-backend marlin`. Did you validate on 2x DGX Spark?

This swap is silent, but it moves `wo_a` to BF16 (about 0.7 GiB more per GPU at TP=2) and can turn off RopeQuant on SM100. Could it log once that `wo_a` falls back to BF16 because the selected linear backend does not keep the DeepGEMM layout?

+    ``deep_gemm_fp8_o_proj`` reads ``wo_a.weight`` directly. Only the DeepGEMM

@@ -600,6 +600,74 @@ def test_mxfp8_bmm_loads_and_projects_grouped_weights(
         torch.testing.assert_close(compiled(inputs), output, rtol=0, atol=0)
 
 
+@pytest.mark.skipif(not current_platform.is_cuda(), reason="DeepSeek V4 needs CUDA")
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("linear_backend", ["marlin", "triton"])
+def test_deepseek_v4_o_proj_with_non_deep_gemm_wo_a(
+    dist_init, default_vllm_config, linear_backend
+):
+    """A wo_a laid out by a non-DeepGEMM backend goes through the BF16 o_proj."""
+    from vllm.model_executor.layers.linear import ColumnParallelLinear
+    from vllm.models.deepseek_v4.nvidia.ops.o_proj import (
+        compute_fp8_einsum_recipe,
+        deep_gemm_fp8_o_proj,
+        maybe_dequant_wo_a,
+    )
+
+    default_vllm_config.model_config = SimpleNamespace(dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    default_vllm_config.kernel_config.linear_backend = linear_backend
+    with torch.device("cuda"):
+        wo_a = ColumnParallelLinear(
+            512,
+            256,
+            bias=False,
+            params_dtype=torch.bfloat16,
+            quant_config=Fp8Config(
+                is_checkpoint_fp8_serialized=True, weight_block_size=[128, 128]
+            ),
+            return_bias=False,
+        )
+    wo_a.is_bmm = True
+    wo_a.bmm_batch_size = 2
+    weight = torch.randn(256, 512, device="cuda").to(torch.float8_e4m3fn)
+    scale = torch.rand(2, 4, device="cuda") + 0.5
+    wo_a.weight.data.copy_(weight)
+    wo_a.weight_scale_inv.data.copy_(scale)
+    wo_a.quant_method.process_weights_after_loading(wo_a)
+    maybe_dequant_wo_a(wo_a)
+
+    num_tokens = 7
+    x = torch.randn(num_tokens, 2, 512, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    # cos = 1, sin = 0 makes the inverse RoPE an identity.
+    cache = torch.cat(
+        (
+            torch.ones(num_tokens, 32, device="cuda"),
+            torch.zeros(num_tokens, 32, device="cuda"),
+        ),
+        dim=1,
+    )
+    recipe, tma_aligned_scales = compute_fp8_einsum_recipe()
+    projected = deep_gemm_fp8_o_proj(
+        x,
+        torch.arange(num_tokens, device="cuda"),
+        cache,
+        wo_a,
+        torch.nn.Identity(),
+        n_groups=2,
+        heads_per_group=1,
+        nope_dim=448,
+        rope_dim=64,
+        o_lora_rank=128,
+        einsum_recipe=recipe,
+        tma_aligned_scales=tma_aligned_scales,
+    )
+    reference_weight = (
+        weight.float().view(2, 128, 4, 128) * scale[:, None, :, None]
+    ).view(2, 128, 512)
+    reference = torch.einsum("tgk,grk->tgr", x.float(), reference_weight)
+    error = (projected.float() - reference.flatten(1)).norm() / reference.norm()
+    assert error < 0.01
+
